eP6_2SpawnAttributeParityAndReaperCoexis.description: the R2/R2b gate -- design section 8, E-P6-2. Two parts, both required.

partA_attributeParity.method: a tiny C/Rust probe child reports its own getpgid(0), sigprocmask, SIGPIPE disposition, open-FD set with FD_CLOEXEC flags, and getcwd; launched via Swift ProcessLauncher.spawn and via the Rust spawner with identical inputs; diff the reports
partA_attributeParity.pass: byte-identical reports across >= 8 configurations (with/without cwd, with/without inherited env keys, deep argv, argv with spaces/UTF-8, missing binary, non-executable binary, binary that execs a shell that forks a grandchild, binary that ignores SIGTERM)

partB_coexistenceSoak.method: in one process, run Rust-supervised children and Swift-supervised children (ProcessTermination-owned) concurrently: 10,000 randomized cycles of spawn / normal-exit / interrupt / SIGTERM-ignoring-child / SIGKILL-escalation / grandchild-orphan / scope-drop-without-shutdown / runtime-identity swap
partB_coexistenceSoak.pass: zero ECHILD on either side's targeted waitpid; zero zombies at quiesce; zero surviving process groups; exit statuses correctly attributed on both sides; zero SIGCHLD handlers installed (asserted via sigaction(SIGCHLD, NULL, &old)); no unbounded thread or FD growth; clean under TSan and ASan

partB_threadScalingR2b.description: absolute count, not a leak check -- a per-child reap thread would show up here as 3N and would still pass every other E-P6-2 criterion, which is the whole point of measuring it

eP6_2SpawnAttributeParityAndReaperCoexis.fail: any status mis-attribution or any surviving group -- a failure means process supervision does not move in this vertical, and P6 reduces to the codec plus an unchanged Swift transport (still-shippable, smaller vertical); this is why E-P6-2 runs before P6-3, not after

eP6_3AdversarialStreamNoDeadlockBoundedM.description: the R3 gate and the instrument retiring the FileHandleChunkChannel hazard -- design section 8, E-P6-3. A synthetic CLI stands in for claude, driven through: max-rate flood (>= 100 MB/s well-formed NDJSON); a single line exceeding the 8 MiB framer cap; a line that stalls mid-object for 30s; stdout closed while stdin writes are pending; exit without EOF; exit while a control request is outstanding; interleaved control_response under flood; a can_use_tool request issued during flood; concatenated/embedded-tail malformed lines under flood; and the deadlock probe -- a child that stops reading its stdin while continuing to write stdout at max rate, with the parent concurrently issuing an interrupt.

pass.a: no deadlock -- the interrupt is acknowledged or times out within its 1.5s deadline in every case, and the reader thread is never observed blocked on a write or on a response
pass.b: peak RSS attributable to the session stays below (framer carry + event queue + resnapshot buffer + per-thread stack reservation, counted explicitly per the 2N+1 E-P6-2 thread budget) + 32 MiB slack
pass.c: zero terminal-class events dropped across the whole matrix (turnCompleted, approvalRequest, interruptOutcome)
pass.d: every induced gap is followed by a successful resnapshot with no transcript corruption
pass.e: the observed maximum per-turn transcript size is recorded and D-8's per-turn resnapshot-buffer cap is set to >= 4x it
pass.f: clean under TSan; zero FD/thread leaks after 1,000 sessions

eP6_3AdversarialStreamNoDeadlockBoundedM.fail: any deadlock, any dropped terminal event, or memory exceeding the declared bound -- returns INV-P6-2 to review
